approach: A `cargo` symlink to the athena binary sits in a per-job wrapper directory that is first on the producer's PATH. When `main` sees argv[0] is `cargo`, it reads the job's slot settings and finds the real cargo further down PATH. For build, check, clippy, test, doc and run it calls `slot_exec::run`, the same function behind the hidden `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` subcommand. `run` takes a producer-class slot from the real `SlotQueue`, appends one JSON line (subcommand, queued_s, slots held) to a per-job log, and runs the command as a plain child in the wrapper's own process group. The child's environment carries `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1`. A wrapper or `build-slot` that sees that marker execs the real cargo with no slot (re-entrancy), so a nested `cargo` inside a slotted `cargo test` cannot wait for a second slot. `run` returns the child's exit code (128+signal if killed). The slot is a file lock, so the OS frees it on any exit, including SIGKILL. A wait past `build_wait_s` prints `no build slot free for <N> s; try again` and exits 75. fmt, metadata and tree exec the real cargo directly. A new optional `Policy.build_wrapper` makes the hook deny a slotted cargo subcommand unless the wrapper file exists AND the first `cargo` on the hook's own PATH is `<wrapper dir>/cargo`; this checks resolution, not only installation. `invoke_and_record` reads and removes the log into a new optional `Invocation.build_slots`. The "build wait" line adds producer commands' waits and the peak slots held, labelled as sampled when a producer command starts (a lower bound). Producer commands only. No unsafe code and no non-Rust file.

decisions.choice: The wrapper is a symlink named `cargo` to the athena binary, dispatched on argv[0] in `main` beside the existing `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` dispatch (main.rs ~546-553). A hidden clap variant `build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` calls the same `slot_exec::run`.
decisions.reason: No shell script is needed (Rust-only default). `-- <cmd>` is the form the design names, and tests and the wrapper share one code path.

rejected.option: A `#!/bin/sh` wrapper script that execs `athena build-slot -- cargo "$@"`
rejected.why: It adds a non-Rust file and needs its own recursion guard.

rejected.option: Having the hook rewrite the command to `athena build-slot -- cargo ...`
rejected.why: It needs new hook output and changes what commands_run holds. The design says a PATH wrapper.

decisions.choice: Re-entrancy (answers finding 11). `run` sets `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1` in the child's environment. `cargo_wrapper` and `build-slot` check it first: if set, they exec the real cargo (or run the command) directly, with no slot and no log line. The name is a constant in athena-agent `lib.rs`.
decisions.reason: The wrapper dir stays first on PATH for everything the wrapped command starts. Repo tests start `cargo` by name (slots.rs:824, run/tests.rs:2659, disk.rs:824, xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:121). With the default max_check_slots = 1 (config.rs:165) a nested cargo would wait for a second slot, hit 75 and fail the producer's test run. The policy denies a command that begins with `NAME=value` (policy.rs:546-553), so a producer cannot set the marker to skip the queue from its own Bash command.

rejected.option: Remove the wrapper dir from the child's PATH
rejected.why: It would have to edit PATH entries by string match. It also stops later nested calls from being logged or checked, and the marker is simpler to test.

rejected.option: Rely on real_cargo skipping the athena binary
rejected.why: That only avoids exec loops; it does not stop a nested call from asking for a slot.

decisions.choice: The child is started with a plain `Command::spawn` in the wrapper's own process group. No `procs::isolate`, no process_group(0) and no signal handler. Exit code is the child's, or 128+signal.
decisions.reason: procs.rs:88-92 `isolate` moves the child to a new group, so group kills (`athena stop` via Registry::stop_all, kill_group on deadline) would reach only the wrapper and not rustc or test binaries. A plain child stays in the agent's group, so group kills reach the whole build tree and the lock dies with the wrapper. `unsafe_code = deny` also rules out a new signal handler outside procs.rs.

rejected.why: It takes the build tree out of the agent's group: a regression the critic found.

rejected.option: Expose a pub parent-death helper in procs.rs
rejected.why: procs.rs is not a deliverable. If the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed, cargo keeps running without a slot; that gap is stated in the Built note. Group kills cover `athena stop` and deadlines.

decisions.choice: The wrapper reads its queue from `{job_dir}/build-slot.json` (slots dir, slots, wait_s, promote_s), named by env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT`. The log path is env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG`. `agent_spec` writes the file for the producer from `jc.config.pipeline()` and `state.slots_dir()`.
decisions.reason: The agent's ATHENA_STATE_DIR is the nested job state (env.rs:97-100), not the repository's, so the wrapper cannot find the shared slots directory alone. A settings file avoids new fields on `EnvSpec`, which is built in about ten places.

rejected.option: Several env variables for the limits
rejected.why: Six values to keep in step; one serde type can be tested.
Forces edits at every EnvSpec literal.

decisions.choice: Slotted subcommands are build, check, clippy, test, doc and run, defined once in athena-agent `lib.rs` and used by the policy and the wrapper. fmt, metadata and tree pass through. A slot is held for the whole run of `cargo run` and `cargo test`, not only the compile; the Built note states this as a known cost (finding 16).
decisions.reason: Design section 4 asks for every cargo command that compiles. The producer may run doc and run (athena.toml:74), so leaving them out would let a build happen outside a slot. Splitting `run` into build-then-exec adds parsing of cargo's arguments for a case the request does not name.

rejected.why: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` compile outside the limit.

decisions.choice: `Policy.build_wrapper: Option<PathBuf>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`). `evaluate` keeps its signature and reads `std::env::var_os("PATH")` once, then calls a new private `evaluate_in(policy, tool, input, cwd, path: Option<&OsStr>)`; `check_bash`, `check_segment` and `check_cargo` gain the `path` argument. In `check_cargo`, when `build_wrapper` is set and `takes_build_slot(sub)`, deny unless `<dir>/cargo` is a file AND the first PATH directory that holds a file named `cargo` is that wrapper dir (compared after canonicalize). decisions.reason: Finding 14: the old denials (`/usr/bin/cargo`, `./cargo`, `+nightly`, `--target-dir`) already pass today and show nothing new. The new rule must catch the real bypass, a different cargo winning PATH. The hook process runs with the agent's environment, so it can resolve `cargo` itself. Tests call `evaluate_in` with a controlled PATH, so no test changes the process environment.

rejected.why: It detects a missing install, not a cargo that resolves elsewhere.

decisions.choice: Keep `commands_run: Vec<String>`. Add a sibling `Invocation.build_slots: Vec<CommandSlot>` with `subcommand`, `queued_s`, `slots_held`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`.

rejected.why: Changes every reader and the old-record read path.

decisions.choice: The peak is carried per producer command as `slots_held`: `Slot::held()` counts the slot files locked just after the slot is won, for any holder class, so checks' slots count. The status line prints the maximum over recorded commands and labels it 'when a producer command started', a lower bound (finding 12). The test that the peak never exceeds the limit measures overlap apart from the lock files: commands write start and end marks to a shared file and the test computes the greatest overlap. A control runs the same commands unwrapped and must show an overlap above the limit, so the instrument can fail. The recorded peak must equal the measured overlap.
decisions.reason: A count over N lock files is at most N by construction, so 'held <= limit' alone cannot fail. An independent overlap measure fails if the queue were skipped. The queue-kept peak file the critic offered would not be readable from `athena status --snapshot`, which reads records, so it is left out.

rejected.option: A peak counter file in the slots dir updated on every win
rejected.why: Stale after SIGKILL; the status snapshot cannot read it; larger change.

decisions.choice: Exit 75 with the documented message is the whole of the timeout handling for producer commands; no hold marker is written. 'The job is held, not failed' is read as: the producer's job is not failed and no attempt is spent, because design section 4 (lines 164-165) gives the decision to the producer, which may retry. Criterion 3's test shows the message is not a policy denial and the wrapper changes no job state; the Built note says plainly that no run-level hold is made.
decisions.reason: Finding 15. The wrapper process has no access to job state: its settings hold only the slots dir and limits. A run-level hold would reach into the step-3 files, which are out of scope.

rejected.option: A run-level test with a fake producer whose command exits 75
rejected.why: A command's exit code never reaches job state in this design; such a test would only repeat the design text.

risks.risk: The host's hook or Bash tool may resolve PATH differently from the environment built here, so `cargo` would run the real cargo unslotted.
risks.mitigation: The hook denies a slotted cargo unless the first `cargo` on its own PATH is the wrapper, so a hook that sees a different PATH fails closed. Whether the hook's PATH equals the Bash tool's is not measured and the Built note says so (open question, Host).

risks.risk: A cargo started inside a slotted command could take a second slot and deadlock or time out.
risks.mitigation: ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD makes nested wrappers pass through; test (e) with slots=1 fails without it. The policy denies `NAME=value` command prefixes (policy.rs:546), so the agent cannot set the marker itself.

risks.risk: If the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed, its child cargo keeps running without a slot.
risks.mitigation: Group kills (athena stop, deadlines) reach the whole tree because the child stays in the agent's group; test (d) checks this. The single-process-kill gap is stated in the Built note.

risks.risk: Counting held slots briefly try-locks free slot files and can make another waiting head miss a slot for one poll (250 ms).
risks.mitigation: The count runs only after a win and is a brief try-lock. The cost is at most one poll of extra wait; tests allow for it and the Built note mentions it.

risks.risk: The recorded peak is sampled only at producer-command starts, so it can undercount moments when only checks won slots.
risks.mitigation: The status line labels it 'when a producer command started'; the Built note calls it a lower bound; the overlap test measures the real concurrency.

risks.risk: Slots held for `cargo run` and `cargo test` last as long as the program runs, which can block checks for up to the Bash timeout (1,200,000 ms, athena.toml:65).
risks.mitigation: Stated as a known cost in the Built note; build_wait_s bounds other waiters (they get 75 or a held check).

risks.risk: A producer that retries in a loop after exit 75 burns its own time, and timed-out waits are not in the record.
risks.mitigation: The message says to try again later; the Built note states that timed-out waits are not recorded.

risks.risk: Struct literals outside the deliverable list (Policy, Invocation) are missed.
risks.mitigation: The edits are listed by file and line; `cargo test --locked` and clippy fail on any missed literal.

risks.risk: The timeout test needs a real wait of at least one second because build_wait_s is in whole seconds.
risks.mitigation: wait_s = 1 and bounded 10 s poll loops; no sleeps order events.

risks.risk: Stale settings or log files from an earlier invocation of the same job (send-back passes).
risks.mitigation: `agent_spec` rewrites the settings and wrapper on each producer invocation, and `invoke_and_record` removes a stale log before the run and the log after it.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/slot_exec.rs, names prefixed `slot_exec_`. Each runs the real athena binary (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")) against a real SlotQueue over the same temp dir with limit 1, and probes with `SlotQueue::try_acquire`. (a) `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- sh -c 'touch started; wait for release'`: after `started` appears try_acquire is None; after release and exit it is Some. (b) A symlink `bin/cargo` to the athena binary and a fake real `cargo` script (written at run time into another temp dir), PATH=bin:real. `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy`, `check` each hold the slot while running and free it after; `cargo fmt --check` does not hold it (try_acquire is Some during it). (c) A command that runs `kill -KILL $$`: wrapper exit code 137 and the slot is free. (d) The wrapper is started in its own process group, running `sh -c 'sleep 30 & sleep 30'`; the test calls `athena_agent::procs::kill_group(pgid, GRACE)` (what `athena stop` does): the slot is free and `group_alive(pgid)` is false within a bounded poll, so the whole tree is gone, not only the direct child. (e) Re-entrancy: with slots=1 and wait_s=5, `build-slot -- sh -c 'cargo build'` with PATH=bin:real finishes with exit 0 well before 5 s; the log has exactly one line (the inner call took no slot).
demonstrations.observes: The slot is held exactly while the command runs and free afterwards; all four subcommands take a slot and fmt does not; a signal death and a group kill both free the slot and end the whole tree; a nested cargo inside a slotted command does not wait for a second slot.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the lock, try_acquire during the command returns Some and 'held' fails. Without release at exit or signal, the probe after returns None. Without the ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD guard, test (e) waits 5 s, exits 75 and fails. With isolate (a new group), (d) would leave the grandchild sleep alive and group_alive stays true.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the `athena build-slot` subcommand and the argv[0]=`cargo` path, both calling `slot_exec::run` (added in steps 3-4). Fixtures: temp state dir, a settings JSON written with `SlotSettings` (step 1), a fake cargo script, injected by PATH and the ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT env in the child's Command. The real SlotQueue is the probe; the only double is the command run, never the queue or the lock. `procs::kill_group` and `group_alive` exist (procs.rs:95-112).

demonstrations.method: Test `slot_exec_second_producer_waits_for_the_first_then_runs`: settings with slots=1. Wrapper A runs `sh -c 'touch a_started; wait for release; touch a_ended'`. After `a_started`, wrapper B (its own ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG file) runs `sh -c 'test -e a_ended && touch b_ran_after_a'`. Poll until `SlotQueue::waiting() == 1`; assert `b_ran_after_a` does not exist. Create `release`; wait for both with a 10 s deadline. Assert `b_ran_after_a` exists, B exited 0, and B's log line has queued_s > 0 and slots_held == 1.
demonstrations.observes: B waits behind A, runs only after A's command ended, and its recorded queued_s is above zero.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the queue, B runs while A still holds the only slot, `a_ended` is absent, `b_ran_after_a` is never created and the test fails. Without the recorded wait, B's queued_s is 0 and the greater-than-zero assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the `athena build-slot` binary run twice. Fixture: a real SlotQueue directory in a temp dir, limit 1, and marker files; order comes from the files, not sleeps. `SlotQueue::waiting()` exists (slots.rs:162). The log line and `SlotSettings` are added in steps 1 and 3.

demonstrations.method: Test `slot_exec_times_out_with_the_documented_message`: slots=1, wait_s=1. Wrapper A holds the slot. Wrapper B runs `cargo test` through the symlink. Assert B exits 75 and stderr is exactly `no build slot free for 1 s; try again`, the fake cargo never ran (no marker), B's log has no line, and `SlotQueue::waiting() == 0` after (the ticket left the queue). Policy test `a_wrapped_cargo_test_is_allowed_by_the_hook` (with wrapper first on the controlled PATH) shows `cargo test` is NoObjection and the 75 message does not contain `Athena policy`. The wrapper has no access to job state (its settings hold only the slots dir and limits) and writes no hold marker; the design leaves the retry to the producer (agent-and-build-slots.md:164-165), as stated in the Built note.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli slot_exec && cargo test -p athena-agent policy
demonstrations.observes: Exit 75 and the exact documented message after the shrunk limit; cargo never ran; the timeout is not a hook denial and leaves no queue entry.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the timeout path, B blocks past the test deadline or runs unslotted. Without exit 75 and the exact text, the assertions fail. The policy test fails if a wrapped `cargo test` were denied.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the `athena build-slot` / symlink binary and `athena_agent::policy::evaluate_in` (added in step 4; `evaluate` and the `bash` test helper exist, policy.rs:90, ~991). Fixture: wait_s=1 in the settings (whole seconds, so about 1 s), a real held slot, and a policy with `build_wrapper: Some(tempdir)` whose `cargo` file is first on the controlled PATH.

demonstrations.method: Env test `the_producers_path_starts_with_the_wrapper_directory`: `env::build` with Side::Produce and a lookup that gives PATH=/usr/bin; assert PATH is `{job_dir}/build-slot-bin:/usr/bin` and the ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT and ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG variables are set; for Side::Verify and Side::Read PATH is unchanged. Policy tests on `evaluate_in` with a tempdir wrapper holding a `cargo` file: (1) CONTROL: with `build_wrapper: None`, `cargo test`, `cargo -q build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` are NoObjection. (2) PROTECTION: with `build_wrapper: Some(dir)` and PATH `dir:/usr/bin`, the same commands are NoObjection; with PATH `other:dir` where `other/cargo` exists they are Deny and the reason names the wrapper and the other cargo; with PATH lacking the wrapper, or PATH None, Deny; with the `cargo` file missing, Deny. (3) CONTROLS that already pass today: `/usr/bin/cargo test`, `./cargo test`, `cargo +nightly build`, `cargo build --target-dir /tmp/t` remain Deny. (4) `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo metadata` are NoObjection even with the wrapper missing or shadowed. (5) An old policy JSON without the key parses with `build_wrapper == None`.
demonstrations.observes: The producer's PATH has the wrapper first; a slotted cargo is allowed only when the first `cargo` on PATH is the wrapper; fmt --check still passes policy.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the PATH change, the env test finds no wrapper first. Without the resolution rule, `cargo test` with another cargo ahead on PATH stays NoObjection and the denial assertion fails. Control (1) shows the same command succeeds without the protection.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `athena_agent::env::build` (exists, env.rs:65, with an injectable lookup) and `athena_agent::policy::evaluate_in` (added in step 4, with a PATH argument so no test edits the process environment); `evaluate` calls it with the real PATH. Fixtures: tempdirs with empty files named `cargo` as wrapper and as a rival. No double stands in for the rule under test.

demonstrations.method: Test groups. (1) records.rs: an old Invocation JSON without `build_slots` reads with an empty list and writes without the key; one with entries round-trips. (2) status.rs: invocations carrying `build_slots` (queued 3.0 and 5.0, slots_held 1 and 2) plus checks with queued_s give a 'build wait' line with `over N check(s) and M producer command(s), longest ... s` and `peak 2 slot(s) held at once when a producer command started`; the existing `over 2 check(s), longest 30.0 s` test stays valid and no recorded waits gives no line. (3) slots.rs unit test: threads take and release slots on a real queue with limit 2 while a shared AtomicUsize counts how many hold a slot at once; assert measured overlap is at most 2 and the largest `Slot::held()` equals it; a control runs the same threads without acquiring and must reach overlap above 2. (4) tests/slot_exec.rs `slot_exec_peak_equals_measured_overlap_and_never_exceeds_the_limit`: slots=2, three wrappers; A and B each wait for the other's start marker so they overlap, C queues behind. Commands append start and end marks to one shared file; the test computes the greatest overlap from it. Assert overlap is 2, C starts after one ended, and the largest slots_held in the three logs equals 2. A control runs two unwrapped commands the same way and must read overlap 2 with limit 1. (5) invocation.rs: with the existing fake driver, the test writes a log file at the path in `spec.env[ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG]` before `invoke_and_record`; the returned record has the parsed `build_slots` and the file is gone.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-data && cargo test -p athena-core status && cargo test -p athena-core slots && cargo test -p athena-core invocation && cargo test -p athena-cli slot_exec
demonstrations.observes: queued_s stored per producer command; old records still read; the status line carries the producer waits and the peak; the peak never passes the limit, measured by overlap apart from the lock files.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, an invocation JSON with build_slots fails to parse (deny_unknown_fields). Without the status change, the line lacks producer and peak text. Without the queue (an unwrapped run), the overlap instrument reads above the limit, so the limit assertion can fail. Without consuming the log, build_slots stays empty.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Throughput::compute(...).text()`, `SlotQueue::acquire` and `Slot::held` (added in step 1), `Athena::invoke_and_record`, `AnyRecord::parse`, and the `athena build-slot` binary. All exist except `Slot::held` and `build_slots`. Fixtures: the status test builders (`landed_job_with_waits` pattern, status.rs:3371) and the Invocation helper (status.rs:2429); a real queue in a temp dir; the invocation.rs fake driver. The test writes the log file; the code that reads it is production code.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the design doc and CHANGELOG. Step 4 of section 8 ends with a 'Built' note stating: the choices (symlink wrapper on argv[0]; settings and log files; the re-entrancy marker; the slotted list including doc and run; `Policy.build_wrapper` with the PATH-resolution check; the sibling `build_slots` field; the per-command peak); the class number (the code's `Class::Producer` is 2, the design counts from 1); why reading.rs, invocation.rs and the literal-only files changed; and what was not measured or is a known cost: priority-tier ordering of producer requests; timed-out waits not recorded and no run-level hold (the producer decides after 75); the peak covers samples at producer commands only (lower bound); `cargo run` and `cargo test` hold a slot for the whole program run; verifier cargo, baseline and reruns unslotted; cargo's children if the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed (a group kill reaches them); whether the host's hook and Bash tool resolve PATH the same way. A CHANGELOG Unreleased entry names the build-slot subcommand, exit 75 message, `build_slots` field and status line.
demonstrations.observes: A 'Built' note under step 4 and a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.
demonstrations.fails_without: No Built note and no changelog line, so the diff for those files is empty.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks on the final tree. This also builds every Policy and Invocation literal and runs `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, which compiles with the new Policy field in its two verifier literals. The corpus covers reading and plan shapes, not tool-policy forms.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, no clippy warnings, formatting clean, only Rust and markdown files changed.
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error from a missed literal or a lint (unused import, too many arguments) fails these.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the three commands. Existing.

open_questions: Host: Does the PreToolUse hook process run with the same PATH that Claude Code's Bash tool gives the commands it runs, or does a shell profile snapshot put another cargo first? Nothing in the repository shows it; the hook's PATH check and the Built note record it as not measured.

User: Should producer requests be ordered by the job's priority tier (urgent, then high, then the rest) as design section 4 describes? The plan leaves this out: the queue has one producer class ordered by time asked, and step 4 of section 8 does not name it.

User: Should the verifier's own cargo commands also be wrapped? They run outside any slot (verifier_commands in athena.toml:76) and the request says producer commands only; the plan leaves them out and says so in the Built note.
